notes: Headline revenue growth is inflated by metal prices. Electronic Materials passes precious-metal cost through to customers; pass-through metal cost almost doubled to $305.7M in Q2 (from $162.7M), so net sales rose 42% while value-added sales rose 15%.

Every segment grew double digits in Q2. Aerospace & defense had its highest quarter ever, with strong growth in semiconductor, industrial, energy and telecom & data-center markets. Materion also won ~$15M of new engine-materials business from a large commercial space customer.
Adjusted EBITDA topped 23% of value-added sales for the first time ($71.8M), helped partly by favorable one-time items.
2026 model: capex ~$75M plus ~$25M for new mine-pit openings at its beryllium operation, D&A ~$75M, interest ~$28M, tax ~14%.
Insiders own ~1.1% of shares. GuruFocus reports $18.6M of insider selling over the past 12 months and no buying.

runContext.title: What kind of company this is, and is it on a Futura list?
runContext.summary: MTRN is not a crypto miner and not a commodity producer under Futura's rules. Its Nasdaq industry is 'Industrial Specialties' (Industrials), which is not on Early Inflection's COMMODITY_INDUSTRIES list, and it is not on the bitcoin-miner list. It does run a beryllium mine in Utah, but it sells engineered alloys and materials rather than raw commodity. It is on none of the three lists today.

runContext.signalsTitle: Why it isn't on a list
signals: Risk It: it passes size, liquidity, coverage (exactly 5 analysts), latest-quarter growth (+42%) and this-year growth (+33%), but next-year consensus revenue growth is +9.2%, just under the 10% minimum. Even if it qualified, its score would be about 45 (TTM growth +21.6% earns little of the 40 growth points and upside is only ~10%), far below the bench cutoff (~65).

Early Inflection: it is in range ($1–30B, $100M+ revenue, 3+ analysts) but scores 60/100 off-screen (today the last pick scores 72 and the last bench name 67): revenue acceleration earns full marks, while falling gross margin, ~10% upside and no AI-bottleneck industry membership hold it down.
Revenue acceleration is partly a metal-price effect: value-added sales grew 15% vs 42% for net sales.
runContext.caveat: Under the current rules it misses Risk It on one threshold (+9.2% vs 10%); that is a rules question for you, not something this page changes.
